structuredReview.summary: Three blockers: an unbounded "nonfunctional rename" escape hatch with no compatibility plan or acceptance coverage, a truth-contract test with no named failing signal (acceptance claims can pass vacuously), and a promotion gate that never runs the regression suite the acceptance criteria depend on. Four nits cover untracked deferral of the integrity gap, missing credential-requirement disclosure, target-vs-current source wording, and freshness-surface acceptance coverage.

findings.title: Unbounded "nonfunctional rename" exception has no scope, compat plan, or acceptance criterion
findings.location: Task 1.1 body: "except where a nonfunctional rename is necessary for truthful public input semantics"
findings.trigger: Implementer renames the setup-wp action input or the legacy package-root name flagged as "package-name drift"; a downstream workflow pinned to the action SHA and passing the old input name starts failing (or silently ignores the input) on the next bump.
findings.impact: A plan that promises unchanged behavior can ship a breaking public contract change to action consumers, with no alias, deprecation window, migration note, or acceptance criterion proving the old name still works.
findings.fix: Name the exact identifiers eligible for rename, and add an acceptance criterion requiring the old name to remain accepted (alias/back-compat) with a documented deprecation note — or drop the rename from this PR entirely and defer it to the qualified action PR.

findings.title: Truth-contract test names a file but no assertion, so every acceptance claim is unverifiable
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance; Promotion Gates: truth-test / test/setup-wp-current-information.test.ts
findings.trigger: Implementer writes a test that asserts a single README substring; the action.yml comments still describe public app-releases downloads and checksum verification, yet the focused gate passes.
findings.impact: The gate this truth-first plan exists to enforce can pass while the false current-state claims it targets remain in the tree; the four doc acceptance items have no failing signal that could ever detect a regression.
findings.fix: State, per acceptance item, the concrete failing signal the test asserts (which file, which required phrase, which forbidden claims — checksum, provenance, arbitrary-version, cache rehash, self-update) and assert against action.yml/workflow text as well as README, so drift in either surface fails.

findings.title: Promotion gates never run the regression suite the acceptance criteria require
findings.location: Promotion Gates table (docs-frontmatter, truth-test) vs Acceptance: "existing workflow/auth tests pass"
findings.trigger: The permitted rename touches an input name consumed by the existing auth/workflow tests; `wp test --files test/setup-wp-current-information.test.ts` passes and `wp audit docs-frontmatter` passes, so the blueprint promotes with a broken suite.
findings.impact: The only functional change this PR allows is exactly the change no gate command exercises; regressions reach merge unblocked.
findings.fix: Add a promotion gate whose command runs the existing workflow/auth test suite (full or explicitly enumerated files) with the expected outcome stated, so the acceptance criterion is gate-enforced rather than prose-only.

findings.title: Deferred integrity/provenance repair has no tracked successor while Residual Unknowns claims None
findings.location: Material Decisions decision-1 ("repair behavior in a later qualified action PR"); Residual Unknowns
findings.trigger: This PR merges, publicly documenting that setup-wp verifies neither checksum nor provenance; no blueprint ID, task, or Produces edge points at the qualifying PR, so the supply-chain gap has no owner or deadline.
findings.impact: A known unverified-download weakness is published and then untracked, and the "unresolved-count: 0" verdict overstates closure.
findings.fix: Reference the successor blueprint/task ID (or add a Residual Unknowns row naming the integrity repair and its owner) in decision-1.

findings.title: Acceptance omits the credential requirement implied by private webpresso/app asset downloads
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 1
findings.trigger: A consumer reads the corrected README, adds setup-wp with the default workflow token, and the download 404s because the release asset lives in a private repo.
findings.impact: The current-truth doc is still incomplete on the one operational detail that makes the current path work; readers hit an opaque failure.
findings.fix: Extend acceptance item 1 to require documenting the token/permission needed to read private webpresso/app release assets today.

findings.title: "Target public product source" framing may read as available today
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 1; Product wedge anchor
findings.trigger: A reader sees app-releases named as "the target public product source" and configures their workflow against it before the qualified action PR lands.
findings.impact: Misconfiguration and support noise during the interim window the plan explicitly creates.
findings.fix: Require the doc to state plainly that app-releases is not yet consumable by this action and must not be configured until the qualified action PR ships.

findings.title: Freshness workflow surface is a stated consuming surface but has no acceptance criterion of its own
findings.location: Product wedge anchor ("freshness workflow guidance") vs Acceptance item 3
findings.trigger: Implementer adds a "deprecated migration debt" line to the README only; agent-kit-freshness.yml keeps its untouched name and comments implying it tracks product updates.
findings.impact: The workflow file itself — the surface a maintainer actually reads when the job fires — keeps the misleading framing this plan exists to correct.
findings.fix: Scope acceptance item 3 to the workflow file's own comments/job naming as well as the README.

structuredReview.summary: Adjudication: 7 prior findings fixed, 0 still open, 0 not-a-blocker. #1 fixed — rename exception gone; Task 1.1 forbids input key/asset/URL/pin changes. #2 fixed — items 1,2,4,5 name inspected files and assertions. #3 fixed — the functional change was removed; item 7 pins exact Bun suites and green PR CI. #4 fixed — decision-1 names `qualify-setup-wp-against-release-a`. #5 fixed — item 1 requires the private-release credential text. #6 fixed — item 3 requires "not consumable/configurable". #7 fixed — item 5 covers the freshness workflow's own name/comments. Dimension walk: feasibility/consistency — nit (decision-2 rationale); dependencies/ownership — no blocker; acceptance criteria — nit (item 3 has no test hook); verification coverage — one new blocker (display-name rename regression path uncovered) plus nits; rollout/compatibility — same blocker; unresolved assumptions — nits only.

findings.title: Authorized workflow/job display-name rename can break workflow_run triggers and required status checks with no covering criterion
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance items 5 and 6 ("the workflow's own name/comments"; "changes only prose/comments/display names")
findings.trigger: Implementer renames `.github/workflows/agent-kit-freshness.yml`'s `name:` (or a job `name:`) to say "deprecated migration debt". Another workflow triggers on `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Kit Freshness"]`, or branch protection requires the old check name: the dependent workflow silently stops firing, or the required check never reports and PR merges block.
findings.impact: A PR the plan declares behavior-neutral changes GitHub-visible identifiers that are load-bearing for triggers, branch protection, badges, and `gh workflow run`. Item 6's ban on "trigger" changes does not catch a break caused indirectly by renaming the referenced workflow, and no gate or named suite asserts the reference set.
findings.fix: Add an acceptance criterion requiring verification that no `workflow_run`/`workflows:` reference, required-status-check name, badge, or `gh workflow` invocation depends on the current workflow/job names — or restrict the freshness correction to comments and README only, leaving `name:` untouched.

findings.title: Acceptance item 3 states a doc requirement with no named failing test signal
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 3
findings.trigger: Items 1, 2, 4, 5 each begin "The focused test ..."; item 3 does not. Implementer omits the app-releases "not consumable / do not configure yet" sentence and the focused contract still passes.
findings.impact: The interim-window warning added in response to prior finding #6 is the only doc claim with no regression signal.
findings.fix: Prefix item 3 with the same "The focused test inspects README.md and action.yml ..." phrasing and name the required phrase.

findings.title: Decision-2's rationale is inconsistent with the gate command it already uses
findings.location: Trust Dossier > Material Decisions, decision-2; Promotion Gates truth-test row
findings.trigger: The truth-test gate runs a Bun test file via `wp test --files test/setup-wp-current-information.test.ts`, so the facade demonstrably executes this repo's Bun contracts; decision-2 nonetheless asserts the trust-gate grammar cannot execute raw Bun as the reason the existing suites cannot be gated.
findings.impact: The stated reason for leaving `test/freshness.test.ts` and `test/workflow-shape.test.ts` outside the promotion gates does not hold, and those suites are the ones most likely to assert the workflow name this task changes.
findings.fix: Either extend the truth-test gate to `wp test --files test/setup-wp-current-information.test.ts test/freshness.test.ts test/workflow-shape.test.ts`, or restate decision-2's rationale accurately (budget, not grammar).

findings.title: Named regression suites have no evidence row establishing they exist under those paths
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 7 (`test/freshness.test.ts`, `test/workflow-shape.test.ts`); Material Claims
findings.trigger: Either file is named differently in the repo; the evidence command errors on a missing path and the implementer substitutes an ad-hoc command.
findings.impact: Required implementation evidence becomes unrunnable as written, weakening the only regression signal for the workflow-name edit.
findings.fix: Add a Material Claims row citing both test paths as evidence, or phrase item 7 as "the existing freshness and workflow-shape suites" with paths as examples.

findings.title: Forbidden-phrase assertions can pass while an equivalent false claim survives in different wording
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance items 2 and 4 ("forbids wording", "rejects README/action claims")
findings.trigger: README says "downloads are validated against the published digest" rather than "checksum"/"provenance"; a substring-based negative assertion passes and the false integrity claim ships.
findings.impact: The negative half of the truth contract is weaker than the positive half; drift in phrasing escapes.
findings.fix: Require items 2 and 4 to also assert positive limitation sentences (e.g. an explicit "no checksum, digest, or provenance verification is performed today" line), so absence is proven by presence.

findings.title: Public-facing docs are required to cite an internal blueprint identifier
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 3 ("must not be selected before `qualify-setup-wp-against-release-a` lands")
findings.trigger: An external consumer reads the README and encounters an internal blueprint ID they cannot look up or track.
findings.impact: Consumer-facing guidance references an opaque internal artifact instead of an observable condition.
findings.fix: Require the doc to state the observable condition ("until this action documents app-releases as supported") and keep the blueprint ID in decision-1 only.

findings.title: Credential input name is asserted in acceptance but not established by any claim evidence
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 1 ("`github-token`/GITHUB_TOKEN"); Material Claims claim-1
findings.trigger: The action's actual input is named differently (e.g. `token`); the doc correction introduces a new inaccurate input name while the focused test asserts it, locking the error in.
findings.impact: A truth-first PR could publish a wrong input identifier — the defect class this plan exists to remove.
findings.fix: Have claim-1 (or a new claim row) name the exact credential input key as read from action.yml, and have item 1 reference that key.

structuredReview.summary: Prior findings: 7 fixed, 0 still open, 0 not a blocker. #1 fixed (item 5 "workflow and job `name:` values remain byte-identical"; item 6 bans display-name changes). #2 fixed (item 3 now begins "The focused test inspects README.md and action descriptions/comments"). #3 fixed (decision-2 cites the "fixed 30-second per-command ceiling", not grammar). #4 fixed (claim-3/claim-4 cite both suite paths). #5 fixed (item 4 "requires positive limitation sentences"). #6 fixed (item 3 uses "until this action itself documents that source as supported"; slug kept in decision-1). #7 fixed (claim-1 names input `github-token` and GITHUB_TOKEN). New: one blocker — asset-name truth is promised in the Summary/wedge anchor but covered by no acceptance criterion or claim row — plus two nits. Dimensions 2 (dependencies/ownership) and 5 (rollout/compatibility) : no blocker.

findings.title: Asset-name truth is a promised deliverable with no acceptance criterion and no evidence row
findings.location: Summary ("legacy package-root names"); Product wedge anchor ("version, source, credentials, asset, pin, and integrity semantics"); Task 1.1 Acceptance items 1-5; Material Claims
findings.trigger: The implementer, following the Summary and wedge anchor, writes an asset-name sentence into README/action.yml descriptions (e.g. "downloads the `wp-<version>.tar.gz` package-root asset") from memory rather than from action.yml. Items 1-5 assert source, credential key, version semantics, limitations, and freshness wording — none inspects the asset identifier — and no Material Claim cites the current asset naming. The focused test passes and a wrong public asset identifier ships.
findings.impact: A truth-first, docs-only PR publishes an unverified consumer-facing artifact identifier — exactly the defect class this blueprint exists to remove — and the wedge anchor's stated "asset" capability lands with no signal that could fail. Uncertain: whether the docs will mention asset names at all, but the Summary and wedge anchor both commit to it.
findings.fix: Add a Material Claim row citing the current asset name(s) as read from `.github/actions/setup-wp/action.yml`, and extend acceptance item 1 to require the focused test to assert that README/action text names those exact current asset identifiers (or drop "asset" from the wedge anchor and "legacy package-root names" from the Summary).

findings.title: Positive-only limitation assertions let a contradictory false claim survive elsewhere in the same file
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance items 2 and 4 ("requires an affirmative sentence"; "requires positive limitation sentences")
findings.trigger: README gains the required "no checksum, digest, or provenance verification is performed today" sentence in a limitations block while an older line in the install section still says "downloads are validated against the published digest". Both positive assertions pass; the contradictory claim ships. Same shape for item 2's npm-version wording.
findings.impact: The prior round's fix replaced the negative assertions rather than adding to them, so the contract now proves presence but no longer disproves the false claims it was written to remove.
findings.fix: Restore the negative half alongside the positive: items 2 and 4 should require both the affirmative limitation sentence and the absence of checksum/digest/provenance/latest-range/self-update/npm-version claims anywhere in the inspected files.

findings.title: "Byte-identical" name requirement is not expressible by the focused test without pinned literal values
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 5 ("workflow and job `name:` values remain byte-identical")
findings.trigger: The implementer writes the focused test with no access to the pre-change file state; "byte-identical to before" cannot be asserted from a single working tree, so the criterion is satisfied vacuously or by a hand-copied literal that may itself be mistyped.
findings.impact: The strongest guard added this round (protecting workflow_run references and required checks) has an ambiguous verification mechanism.
findings.fix: Restate item 5 as: the focused test pins the exact current workflow and job `name:` string literals read from `.github/workflows/agent-kit-freshness.yml`, and the diff review confirms those lines are untouched.

structuredReview.summary: Prior findings: 3 fixed, 0 still open, 0 not a blocker. #1 fixed (claim-2 plus acceptance item 4 pin wp-linux-x64/arm64, wp-darwin-arm64, agent-kit-package.tgz from action.yml); #2 fixed (items 2 and 5 now require positive statements AND reject contradictory wording anywhere inspected); #3 fixed (item 6 pins literals plus diff confirmation). Dimension walk: (1) feasibility/internal consistency — one blocker (item 2's blanket npm-version/latest rejection contradicts item 6's required npm freshness prose); (2) dependencies/sequencing/ownership — no blocker; (3) acceptance proving stated behavior — one blocker (limitation and unsupported-source truths have no evidence row); (4) verification success/failure/regression — no blocker, one nit; (5) rollout/compatibility/cleanup — no blocker; (6) unresolved assumptions — no blocker.

findings.title: Blanket rejection of npm-version/range/latest wording contradicts the required npm freshness prose in the same inspected files
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance items 2 and 6 ("rejecting contradictory npm-version/range/latest wording anywhere inspected" vs "call npm agent-kit scanning deprecated migration debt")
findings.trigger: Item 6 requires README/freshness comments to describe the deprecated npm scanner, whose only accurate description mentions npm versions, e.g. "this workflow compares the latest published @webpresso/agent-kit npm version against the pinned one". Item 2's rejection scope is "anywhere inspected", which includes that same README and those same comments, so the focused test fails on the very sentence item 6 mandates.
findings.impact: The two acceptance criteria cannot both be satisfied. The implementer resolves the deadlock by deleting or vaguening the accurate freshness/migration-debt prose (a stated deliverable), or by weakening the rejection until it no longer catches the false "version is an npm version" claim it exists to remove.
findings.fix: Scope item 2's rejection to statements about the setup-wp `version` input and its source/selection semantics, explicitly exempting text that describes the deprecated `@webpresso/agent-kit` npm freshness scanner required by item 6.

findings.title: Limitation and unsupported-source truths are mandated as doc text with no Material Claim grounding them in the action source
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance items 3 and 5; Trust Dossier > Material Claims (claim-1..claim-5)
findings.trigger: Following item 5 the implementer writes "no checksum, digest, or provenance verification, no cache rehash, and no wp self-update is performed today", and following item 3 "`webpresso/app-releases` is not supported or configurable today". No Material Claim cites action.yml for the absence of integrity checks, cache rehash, self-update, or app-releases support, so those sentences come from the blueprint's memory. If the action already re-hashes the cache key or verifies a digest, the focused test still passes: it only asserts the sentence is present and that no contradicting sentence exists.
findings.impact: A truth-first, docs-only PR publishes new consumer-facing security and behavior statements that no named signal can falsify — the same defect class as the previously accepted asset-name blocker, now on the plan's largest claim surface.
findings.fix: Add Material Claim rows citing `.github/actions/setup-wp/action.yml` (and the freshness workflow where relevant) as the read source for: absence of checksum/digest/provenance verification, absence of range/latest selection, cache behavior without rehash, absence of wp self-update, and absence of any `webpresso/app-releases` code path; require items 3 and 5 to be written from those cited lines.

findings.title: Pinned workflow and job name literals have no evidence row
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 6 (`Reusable agent-kit freshness`, `agent-kit-freshness`); Material Claims claim-3
findings.trigger: Either literal is mistranscribed in the blueprint; the focused test then fails against a correct repository. The quoted job name is identical to the workflow filename stem, a common transcription slip.
findings.impact: Wasted implementation cycle and pressure to reconcile the mismatch; the rename risk itself is contained by item 7 and the diff check.
findings.fix: Extend claim-3 (or add a row) to cite the exact workflow and job `name:` values as read from `.github/workflows/agent-kit-freshness.yml`, and state that on mismatch the blueprint literal is corrected, never the workflow.

findings.title: Guidance that the default `github.token` may be insufficient was dropped from acceptance item 1
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 1 ("the need for a token that can read private assets")
findings.trigger: Docs satisfy item 1 with "provide a token that can read private assets" without saying the workflow-default `github.token` cannot read another repository's private release assets, so a consumer wires the default and hits a 404 at install time.
findings.impact: The most common operational failure mode for this action stays undocumented, though the general requirement is still asserted.
findings.fix: Restore the prior clause: docs must state the default `github.token` is insufficient for cross-repository private assets and a caller-supplied token is required.

findings.title: Existing Bun suites are required as evidence but no runnable command is named
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 8 ("exact existing freshness and workflow-shape Bun suites pass as task evidence/PR CI")
findings.trigger: At verification time the implementer must produce evidence for both suites, but the plan names only the `wp test --files` command for the focused contract.
findings.impact: Evidence for the regression suites is unreproducible without guessing the invocation.
findings.fix: Name the exact command (e.g. `bun test test/freshness.test.ts test/workflow-shape.test.ts`) in item 8.

structuredReview.summary: Adjudication: 5 prior findings fixed, 0 still open, 0 not a blocker. #1 fixed (item 2 scopes negative npm checks to setup-wp `version`/source selection and exempts freshness-scanner prose); #2 fixed (claim-3 cites action.yml for absent app-releases path, integrity, range/latest, cache, self-update); #3 fixed (claim-4 pins exact workflow/job names from the freshness YAML; item 6 corrects blueprint literals on mismatch); #4 fixed (item 1 requires the default `github.token` cross-repo limitation and a caller-supplied token); #5 fixed (item 8 names `bun test test/freshness.test.ts test/workflow-shape.test.ts`). Dimensions: feasibility, sequencing/ownership, regression evidence, rollout/cleanup, open assumptions — no blocker. Two new blockers come from this round's compression: the source-repository literal was dropped from the pinned truths, and the cache-behavior claim was widened inconsistently across Summary, item 5, and claim-3.

findings.title: Source repository literal is no longer pinned or claimed, so docs can name the wrong asset source and still pass
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance items 1 and 3 ("name private app exact tags", "app-releases is unsupported"); Material Claims claim-1
findings.trigger: The implementer writes README text "binaries are downloaded from exact tags of the private app repository" without naming `webpresso/app`, or names a wrong repo. Item 1 only requires "private app exact tags", item 4 pins asset filenames but not the source repo, and no Material Claim cites action.yml for the download repository, so the focused test passes.
findings.impact: The plan's core deliverable is truthful source and credential semantics for a private, token-gated download. Consumer-facing docs can publish an unnamed or incorrect source repository, and the credential guidance in item 1 (which token can read which repo's assets) becomes unactionable. Item 3's app-releases rejection is also weakened to a bare unqualified substring.
findings.fix: Restore the exact literals: item 1 must require README/action text to name `webpresso/app` exact tags, item 3 must use `webpresso/app-releases`, and extend claim-1 to cite `.github/actions/setup-wp/action.yml` as the read source for the download repository, applying the same blueprint-literal-yields-to-source rule used in item 6.

findings.title: Cache-behavior truth is stated three different ways and the widest form may be a false published claim
findings.location: Summary ("no ... cache revalidation"); Task 1.1 Acceptance item 5 ("no ... cache persistence or rehash/revalidation"); Material Claims claim-3 ("no ... cache persistence/rehash")
findings.trigger: The action caches the downloaded wp binary (tool cache or actions/cache) but never revalidates it. Item 5 then mandates a doc sentence asserting "no cache persistence", which is false, and the focused test only checks that the mandated sentence is present and unopposed, so the false statement ships. If the implementer instead writes the truthful "cache is persisted but never revalidated", that sentence contradicts item 5 and the gate fails.
findings.impact: Either a false behavior statement is published to consumers by a truth-first PR, or the acceptance criterion is unsatisfiable against a correct repository. The three internal wordings disagree, so no single reading of the plan is authoritative for the implementer or the test author.
findings.fix: Pick one scope grounded in what `action.yml` shows and use it identically in the Summary, item 5, and claim-3 — recommended: assert only the absence of cache rehash/revalidation, and require docs to describe any cache persistence that does exist truthfully rather than deny it.

findings.title: claim-1 says "caller token fallback" where the acceptance criterion says a caller token is required
findings.location: Trust Dossier > Material Claims claim-1
findings.trigger: An implementer reading claim-1 documents `github-token` as having a caller-token fallback, implying graceful degradation, while item 1 requires stating that the default `github.token` normally cannot read cross-repository private assets and a caller-supplied token with access is required.
findings.impact: Mildly conflicting credential guidance between the evidence row and the acceptance criterion; the acceptance text governs, so the shipped docs are unlikely to be wrong.
findings.fix: Reword claim-1 to match item 1: `github-token` maps to GITHUB_TOKEN and must be a caller-supplied token with read access to the private release assets.

structuredReview.summary: Prior findings: 3 fixed, 0 still open, 0 not-a-blocker. #1 fixed — item 1 requires exact `webpresso/app`, item 3 requires `webpresso/app-releases`, claim-1 cites action.yml for the source repo with the literal-yields-to-source rule. #2 fixed — Summary, item 5, and claim-3 now use one identical wording ("no cache store/restore path or rehash/revalidation guarantee; downloads on every invocation") grounded in claim-3's action.yml evidence. #3 fixed — claim-1 now states a caller-supplied token with private release-read access is required. Dimension walk: (1) consistency — no blocker; (2) dependencies/ownership — no blocker; (3) acceptance criteria — no blocker, one enumeration nit; (4) verification coverage — no blocker, one grounding nit; (5) rollout/compatibility — no blocker; (6) unresolved assumptions — no blocker. Two non-blocking nits remain.

findings.title: Item 4 dropped the "no invented current asset" rejection, so extra unsupported asset names can pass
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 4 (asset pins)
findings.trigger: An implementer writes README text listing `wp-linux-x64`, `wp-linux-arm64`, `wp-darwin-arm64` plus a nonexistent `wp-windows-x64`; the test only checks the pinned names are present, so the untruthful extra asset ships.
findings.impact: A truth-correction PR can publish an asset the action never downloads. Bounded because item 5's contradiction rejection and item 4's source-derived pins still cover the main cases, and this is a case to add to a test not yet written.
findings.fix: Restore the removed clause in item 4: the focused test must also reject asset names absent from the action source's selection logic.

findings.title: Cache/download statements in item 5 are not tied to action source the way item 4's pins are
findings.location: Task 1.1 Acceptance item 5; Material Claims claim-3
findings.trigger: If action.yml in fact places the binary in a tool cache, the mandated sentence "no cache store/restore path ... downloads on every invocation" is false, and a presence-only text assertion still passes.
findings.impact: Residual risk of publishing an inaccurate behavioral statement; claim-3 now grounds it in action.yml, so this is a grounding-strength refinement, not a demonstrated contradiction. Uncertain because the action source is not available to this review.
findings.fix: Add to item 5 the rule item 4 uses: derive cache/download statements from action source, correcting blueprint wording rather than source if evidence disagrees.

structuredReview.summary: One blocker: Summary pins executable truth to 36b412a while D1 names exact current main, with no precedence rule if they diverge; two verification/evidence nits remain.

findings.title: Conflicting executable-truth authority
findings.location: Summary; Trust Dossier Material Decisions D1
findings.trigger: An implementer starts the task when main no longer equals 36b412a, or when those two phrasings are read as different authorities today.
findings.impact: README and the parity test can be grounded on different snapshots, recreating the concurrent-source-advance failure D1 exists to prevent, or blocking on irreconcilable acceptance literals versus source.
findings.fix: State one authority rule in both places (pin 36b412a, or main-at-task-start with mandatory re-check of plan literals if setup-wp/freshness paths changed) and say source wins over embedded acceptance names on drift.

findings.title: Promotion gates omit required suite runs
findings.location: Trust Dossier Promotion Gates; Task 1.1 Acceptance
findings.trigger: A controller treats Promotion Gates as the full pre-merge bar and runs only the focused truth contract plus format check.
findings.impact: Acceptance still requires existing setup-wp/freshness/workflow suites, so gate config and task proof can disagree on what must be green.
findings.fix: Add those existing suite commands to Promotion Gates with the same expected pass outcome already stated in acceptance.

findings.title: C6 evidence under-cites action lock
findings.location: Trust Dossier Material Claims C6
findings.trigger: A reviewer opens only the cited freshness.test.ts to validate C6’s claim that existing suites lock action and freshness behavior.
findings.impact: The action half of C6 is not evidenced at the claim’s own citation even though C2 points at setup-wp tests elsewhere.
findings.fix: Cite both test/setup-wp.test.ts and test/freshness.test.ts on C6, or narrow C6’s wording to freshness only.
